title: Global Key Themes 2027
gist: Oxford Economics' short research-briefing teaser says the world economy is on track for 2.7% growth in 2026 (matching its December forecast) and should pick up to 3.0% in 2027, with the outcome hinging on three themes: the AI boom will not turn to bust despite the recent stock wobble, inflation will grind lower as oil returns to its pre-war path without prompting a dovish central-bank pivot, and AI-driven investment will keep bond yields elevated.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics estimates the world economy is on track to have expanded by 2.7% in 2026 despite volatility, in line with the forecast it made in December 2025.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Global growth absorbed 2026 shocks without derailing; resilience is the base case rather than a recession call.
insights.quote: Despite all the tumult, the world economy looks on track to have expanded by 2.7% in 2026, which is in line with our forecast from last December.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts a modest pick-up in world GDP growth to 3.0% in 2027, from 2.7% in 2026.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: A mild global acceleration supports cyclical exposure in 2027, but the forecast is explicitly contingent on the durability of the AI boom.
insights.quote: For 2027, we expect a modest pick-up in world GDP growth to 3.0%

insights.claim: Oxford Economics argues the AI boom will not turn to bust in 2027 and that the recent stock market wobble is probably not the beginning of the end, making AI durability the swing factor between strong and much weaker global growth.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Treat the recent tech/AI equity sell-off as a wobble rather than a regime change in the base case, but recognise global growth is levered to AI capex continuing.
insights.quote: The recent stock market wobble probably isn’t the beginning of the end.
insights.locator: Theme 1: The AI boom won’t turn to bust

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects the oil price to gradually decline to its pre-war path in 2027, helping inflation grind lower.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: A gradual unwind of the war-related oil premium argues against positioning for a renewed energy-price spike in the base case.
insights.quote: We expect the oil price to gradually decline to its pre-war path in 2027.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics judges that falling inflation in 2027 is unlikely to trigger a dovish pivot by central banks.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Do not price aggressive rate cuts on the back of disinflation; policy rates likely stay restrictive for longer.
insights.quote: But this is unlikely to trigger a dovish pivot by central banks.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics identifies the AI boom as a key driver of the 2026 rise in bond yields and expects it to keep yields elevated in 2027.
insights.speaker: Anusha Suthenthiran
insights.so_what: Duration is exposed to AI investment demand: a durable AI boom implies sticky high yields, while an AI bust would be the main route to a yield rally.
insights.quote: The AI boom has been a key driver of this year’s rise in yields and should keep them elevated in 2027.
insights.locator: Theme 3: AI will dictate the path for bond yields
